post.instagram:
Send this to the parent who is tired of saying the same rule twice a day.

You set a rule. They never agreed to it. So every time you hold the line, it is a fresh argument, and you are the one who has to win it.

A rule they did not agree to is a rule you have to enforce twice a day.

So we made the family agreement:

1. Pick the one for their age, from first screens to nearly independent.
2. Choose the promises together, at the table. Bedtime, where devices sleep, new apps and games.
3. You both sign it, then print it for the fridge.
4. It sits on their own app too, so nobody has to remember what was said.
5. They can ask to change it, with a reason, and you decide.

If a phone or a console is on a Christmas list at your house, the deal is easier to write before the wrapping paper comes off than after.

Which rule at your house gets argued about the most?

What stage is your child? Three questions, no sign up, link in bio.
